chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawaffali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The meat of the jalalah chicken is not to be eaten until it is tied up (confined) for three days, and the jalalah duck for five days, and the jalalah sheep for ten days, and the jalalah cow for twenty days, and the jalalah camel for forty days.
ai.seo_question: What are the confinement periods for different jalalah animals to make their meat halal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar details the specific purification periods for 'jalalah' animals—those fed on impure substances—ranging from three days for poultry to forty days for camels, reflecting the gradual elimination of impurities from their flesh. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on physical purity in dietary laws, linking the animal's diet directly to the spiritual and physical state of the consumer.
